etymologies.etymologyHTML: From popular +‎ -ity, from Latin popularitas (“an effort to please the people”).

definitions.definition: The quality or state of being popular; especially, the state of being esteemed by, or of being in favor with, the people at large
(archaic) The quality or state of being adapted or pleasing to common, poor, or vulgar people

quote.citation: 1600, Ben Jonson, Every Man Out of His Humour:
quote.text: So this Gallant, labouring to avoid Popularity, falls into a habit of Affectation, Ten thousand times hatefuller than the former.

definitions.definition: (archaic) Something which obtains, or is intended to obtain, the favor of the vulgar; claptrap.

quote.citation: 1597, Francis Bacon, The Colours or Good and Evil:
quote.text: Popularities, and circumstances which  […]  sway the ordinary judgment.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) The act of courting the favour of the people.

quote.citation: 1603, Plutarch, translated by Philemon Holland, Moralia:
quote.text: Cato (the younger) charged Muraena, and indicted him in open court for popularity and ambition.

quote.citation: 1834–1874, George Bancroft, History of the United States, from the Discovery of the American Continent, volume (please specify |volume=I to X), Boston, Mass.: Little, Brown and Company [et al.], →OCLC:
quote.text: A little time be allowed for the madness of popularity to cease.
